description: The pandas differences between ryo and the pinned Ruff 0.16.5 that Ruff parity accepts, each pinned by finding. The Ruff benchmark's parity command (asymptote tool bench-parity/python/ruff) reads this file and refuses it before either contestant runs for a request whose corpus digest (its file list and sealed context entries, as the benchmark's canonical text spells them) differs, or when a rule is named twice. Any unmatched finding not named here, any named finding that no longer occurs and any end-position difference fails the run.

differences.reason: pandas/io/stata.py writes in loops through bio = BytesIO() (from io import BytesIO). The pinned Ruff 0.16.5 treats only open(), io.open(), io.open_code(), os.open() and pathlib.Path(...).open() initializers as IO objects, so it omits these loops, although its documentation says the rule checks for IOBase.write in a for loop; ryo reports them under the same certified reference discrepancy as Django's io.StringIO loops, io-binding-4 in rules/FURB122/cases.toml, whose CPython 3.10 evidence (profiles/FURB122/evidence/independent-io-cpython310.json) shows io.StringIO is an IOBase stream with write and writelines; io.BytesIO is the BufferedIOBase stream of the same io module, which rules/FURB122 lists among its IO factories.
